meta.title: Can You Understand British Money Slang? 🇬🇧

sentences.text: In England, we don't say fifty pounds. We call this fifty quid.
Money appears all the time in daily conversation.
For example, Hey man, have you got a tenner on you?
Sorry lad, I've only got a fiver.
If you don't understand that, then you are missing a very big chunk of British life.
In this video, I'll teach you what nobody teaches you about money.
This is a one pound coin, but what do British people call it? We call it a quid.
One quid equals one pound. But what if there are two? We don't say quids, there is no s,
so it's just one quid, two quid, three quid, four quid. But what about five quid?
Five quid is a fiver. This is a five pound note. What can you buy with a fiver in England?
A meal deal. A tuna sandwich, a can of coke and a bag of crisps.
Meal deals are a huge cultural phenomenon in England. They are very popular. Every day, millions of people walk into a Tesco and pick up a sad little sandwich, a bag of crisps and a drink.
and they feel genuinely good about it.

A 20er?
Nope we just call it 20 quid The most common term for is a grand and you might hear it in a conversation
like, Hey Rock, how much is your rent in London?

Do you fancy a pint then?
Mate, I'm skint.
You might know the word broke, which is the standard universal term for having little money.
But in Britain, we like to do things differently.
We say skint.
I'm skint.
It means I've got very little money.
Skint is a top slang word in the UK.
All right, mate, you look a bit rough.
I'm skint, mate.

I am loaded.

That's a bargain.
